title: SNAKE_CASE turns a flat scalar field into a nested object
rationale: transformKeys runs applyNamingStrategy over the ALREADY-ENCODED flat key. SNAKE_CASE inserts bare separator characters into a string whose separators are structural. The decoder cannot distinguish them, so the injected underscore becomes a nesting level that did not exist in the source.
catchesBugClass: Post-encode key rewriting that is not encoding-aware. The fix is either to apply naming strategies to segments before encoding or to re-escape after transforming; this fixture fails until one of those happens and passes for either.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the reverse damage from the SNAKE_CASE underscore-run collapse, because this document has no runs. A source name with adjacent capitals or containing __ would exercise that and could destroy structure a different way.

predicted.detail: A scalar at depth 1 is reconstructed as an object at depth 2. Case-folding is a requested transform and would be ACCEPTED_LOSS on its own; inventing structure is not.
